images.title: The test for a statistical question
images.purpose: Give a compact recap of the one test used to sort questions: will the answers vary?
images.composition: A small decision diagram centred in the frame: one question box at the top, two arrows down to two result boxes, with generous white space.
exact_structure: One rounded box at the top centre, outlined in reddish purple (#CC79A7), reading Will the answers vary?
Exactly 2 arrows leave the box downward: the left arrow labelled Yes, the right arrow labelled No.
The left arrow ends at a green (#009E73) filled rounded box reading Statistical, with a cluster of 4 small dots of different heights drawn inside it to suggest varying data.
The right arrow ends at a vermilion (#D55E00) filled rounded box reading Not statistical, with exactly 1 small dot drawn inside it.
rejection: Yes leading to Not statistical, or No leading to Statistical
more than 3 boxes or more than 2 arrows
example questions written in the frame
images.takeaway: Ask whether the answers will vary: if yes the question is statistical, if no it is not.
images.description: A decision diagram: the box Will the answers vary? leads by Yes to a green Statistical box and by No to a vermilion Not statistical box.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Use it as the check to run on every question card before sorting it.

image_decisions.why: A one step decision diagram recaps the sorting rule for the practice.
